title: Design search autocomplete / typeahead
relevance: High — Alex Xu Vol.1 ch.13 classic; asked standalone and as the suggestion box inside Search / e-commerce / Maps designs (campus + experienced; Google, Meta, Amazon, LinkedIn, Uber, Flipkart, Databricks).
company_notes: Campus/intern/new-grad: very common as Design autocomplete / typeahead / Google search suggestions, and as the suggestion box inside Amazon / Flipkart / YouTube designs. Experienced (1–4+ YOE): deeper on sharding, atomic index swap, trending overlay, personalization vs cache, ES/FST vs custom trie, multi-locale — Meta, Google, Amazon, LinkedIn, Uber, Databricks. High frequency Alex Xu Vol.1 ch.13 staple and standard top-K + prefix index probe.

phases.goal: Clarify product scope (prefix suggestions vs full search), FRs/NFRs, and what is out of MVP.

must_hit.point: Functional MVP: as the user types, return top 5 queries that start with the prefix, ranked by historical search frequency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States prefix-start match, top 5, and frequency ranking as the Alex Xu-style MVP.

must_hit.point: NFR: perceived p99 under ~100 ms (UI stutters above ~100 ms), high availability; eventual consistency OK so suggestions can lag hours.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names ~100 ms latency / stutter folklore and accepts hours of suggestion lag.

must_hit.point: Clarify first: prefix-only vs infix, K, typo/spellcheck, personalization, languages, case/charset; English lowercase-only and no spellcheck in MVP unless asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the clarifying questions and parks typo/personalization/multi-locale for later.

must_hit.point: Out of scope unless asked: full web search ranking, ads, rich entity cards, Maps geocode — this is the suggestion box, not the results page.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws a hard line between typeahead suggestions and full search / Maps / ads.

probes: What are you building — Google-bar query suggestions or full search — and which FRs/NFRs are in the MVP?
Is ranking frequency-only, and are typos or personalization in scope?

hints.1: Separate the suggestion box from the full search results page before listing features.
hints.2: Lock top-K prefix completions, frequency rank, ~100 ms latency, and eventual consistency.
hints.3: MVP: top 5 prefix-start completions by historical frequency, English lowercase, no spellcheck; p99 < ~100 ms; lag of hours OK; park full ranking/ads/Maps.

phases.goal: State Alex Xu–style DAU/QPS assumptions aloud and note how debounce changes load.

must_hit.point: Example scale: ~10M DAU, ~10 searches per user per day, ~20 AJAX calls per search without debounce → ~24k average QPS and ~48k peak QPS (~2×).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says 10M DAU → ~24k / ~48k QPS with the searches-per-day and chars-per-query assumptions.

must_hit.point: Client debounce (~100–300 ms) cuts QPS a lot; still design for tens of kQPS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions debounce as a QPS reducer while keeping tens-of-kQPS in the design target.

must_hit.point: New unique query storage ~0.4 GB/day raw strings; serving index size is dominated by trie / prefix→top-K, not raw logs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates warehouse log growth (~0.4 GB/day) from the in-memory serving index.

probes: Walk through DAU to QPS for typeahead — what happens if the client does not debounce?
Where does storage actually go — logs or the serving index?

hints.1: Start from DAU × searches/day × keystrokes, then peak multiplier.
hints.2: Call out debounce vs raw keystroke QPS, and serving index vs log warehouse.
hints.3: 10M DAU × 10 × ~20 / day → ~24k avg / ~48k peak; debounce drops QPS; ~0.4 GB/day raw strings; serving trie dominates memory.

phases.goal: Define a public suggest read API and keep analytics off the hot path.

must_hit.point: Public suggest API: GET /v1/suggest?prefix=...&limit=...&locale=... returning suggestions as {query, score} list.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches REST suggest with prefix, limit, locale and a scored suggestions array.

must_hit.point: Optional Authorization/session for personalized re-rank; If-None-Match / short Cache-Control for CDN.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions cache validators/CDN headers and optional auth for personalization.

must_hit.point: Search submit / click-through analytics are async log pipeline events — not on the suggest path; admin rebuild/blocklist is not the interview focus.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps logging and admin APIs off the keystroke critical path.

probes: What does the suggest endpoint look like, and what stays off that path?
How would CDN caching interact with personalized suggestions?

hints.1: One read API for suggestions; logging is separate.
hints.2: Include prefix/limit/locale and scored results; mention CDN cache headers.
hints.3: GET /v1/suggest?prefix&limit&locale → {suggestions:[{query,score}]}; analytics async; optional session + Cache-Control.

phases.goal: Separate append-only logs, aggregated frequencies, and a versioned serving index (trie or KV).

must_hit.point: Query log event (append-only): {query, user_id?, locale, ts, session_id?}; frequency table: {normalized_query, count_window, locale}.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names an append-only log and an aggregated frequency table after batch/stream aggregate.

must_hit.point: Serving index: trie node with children[char] and topK:[(query,score)] size ≤ K at build time, OR KV key=prefix (or locale:prefix) → ordered top-K.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks trie-with-topK-per-node or materialized prefix→top-K and sticks to it.

must_hit.point: Version with index_version / snapshot id and atomic pointer flip so servers never serve a half-built trie.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes snapshot versioning and atomic swap for safe deploys.

must_hit.point: Optional: trending:{prefix} Redis ZSET speed-layer overlay; user_recent_queries for personalization.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds optional overlay/personalization structures without putting them on every write.

probes: What data do you store for logs vs what the suggest servers actually read?
How do you roll out a new trie without serving a half-built index?

hints.1: Logs and frequency aggregates are not the online lookup structure.
hints.2: Serving = trie top-K per node or prefix→top-K KV, plus a versioned atomic flip.
hints.3: Append-only log → frequency table → immutable trie/KV with top-K; index_version + atomic pointer; optional trending ZSET.

phases.goal: Split online suggest path from offline aggregate/rebuild, with caching layers on the hot path.

must_hit.point: Two timelines: online read path (keystroke → suggestions) vs offline/async write path (logs → aggregate → rebuild index); never mutate a shared trie on every search under read load.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly separates read and write timelines and forbids sync trie mutation on search.

must_hit.point: Online path: client debounce → CDN/edge → Suggest API/LB → in-memory trie/prefix servers (sharded by prefix) → Redis for hot prefixes; walk trie then return precomputed top-K.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws debounce → CDN → API → RAM trie shards → Redis and a walk+return (no DFS sort).

must_hit.point: Cold path: search submit → Kafka → aggregator (Spark/Flink batch ± stream) → frequency table → trie builder → object-storage snapshot → push/pull → atomic swap on suggest servers (+ optional Redis trending overlay).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes Kafka→aggregate→build→snapshot→atomic swap, pipeline never blocking keystrokes.

must_hit.point: Path-B alternative: Elasticsearch completion suggester (in-memory FST) instead of a custom trie — simpler ops, slightly higher latency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names ES completion / FST as the managed alternative to owning trie sharding.

probes: Sketch the online path vs the offline rebuild path.
Where do CDN, Redis, and the in-memory trie sit relative to each other?

hints.1: Keystrokes never wait on log aggregation.
hints.2: Debounce + CDN/Redis in front of sharded RAM tries; Kafka rebuild with atomic swap.
hints.3: Client debounce→CDN→API→sharded trie (+Redis hot); Kafka→aggregate→immutable trie snapshot→atomic swap; optional ES completion Path-B.

phases.goal: Defend precomputed top-K, freshness hybrid, personalization vs cache, and custom trie vs ES.

must_hit.point: Query-time DFS + heap on every keystroke blows p99 on short prefixes; store top-K on every trie node (or materialize prefix→top-K) at build time so the read path is walk + return.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects subtree DFS on the hot path and commits to precomputed top-K per node/prefix.

must_hit.point: Freshness vs latency: do not update the trie on every search; batch rebuild alone goes stale on viral trends; hybrid = immutable trie for >99% + streaming trending overlay merge at query time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States batch vs realtime and the immutable-trie + streaming overlay hybrid.

must_hit.point: Personalization: global top-K is CDN-friendly; personalized results fragment caches — fetch global top-N then re-rank with user history in a few ms, or only on miss / logged-in path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains cache fragmentation and re-rank-after-global-fetch pattern.

must_hit.point: Custom trie: lowest latency and full control but you own sharding/deploy; ES completion FST: faster to ship with fuzzy/context options if the cluster already exists.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares latency/control of custom trie vs ship-speed of ES completion.

probes: What happens to latency if you DFS the subtree under prefix "a" on every keystroke?
How do you get trending freshness without mutating the trie on every search?
Custom in-memory trie or Elasticsearch completion — when would you pick each?

hints.1: The hot path should not sort a large subtree.
hints.2: Precompute top-K; use batch + optional stream overlay; keep personalization off the CDN path.
hints.3: Top-K on every node; immutable trie + Kafka/Flink/Redis trending overlay; global then light re-rank; custom trie vs ES FST Path-B.

phases.goal: Scale QPS and memory, handle hot short prefixes, and deploy rebuilds safely.

must_hit.point: QPS: debounce + CDN/Redis for power-law head prefixes; horizontally scale the stateless suggest tier.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names debounce/CDN/Redis for popular prefixes and horizontal suggest scaling.

must_hit.point: Hot prefixes (1–2 chars) almost always cached; optionally require min prefix length (e.g. 2–3) before hitting origin; full English query trie can be tens of GB → shard by prefix range and replicate.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Handles short-prefix heat and memory via caching, min length, and prefix sharding.

must_hit.point: Rebuild deploy: blue/green or versioned snapshot + atomic flip; rolling reload so not all hosts GC at once.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes safe index cutover without fleet-wide GC spike.

must_hit.point: Pipeline lag / poison trends: windowed counts + uniqueness checks; kill switch to disable overlay; multi-region serve nearest snapshot replica (global exact ranking not required).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Covers trending abuse controls and multi-region replica serving.

probes: What saturates first — QPS on short prefixes or trie memory — and how do you shard?
How do you roll a new index without taking the fleet down?

hints.1: Short prefixes and trie RAM are the usual pain points.
hints.2: Cache/min-length for hot prefixes; shard by prefix; atomic snapshot flip.
hints.3: Debounce+CDN/Redis; cache 1–2 char prefixes; shard tens-of-GB trie by prefix; blue/green atomic flip; overlay kill switch.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Naive DFS subtree + heap on every keystroke blows p99 on short prefixes. Interview answer: store top-K on every node (or materialize prefix→top-K) at build time; read path is walk + return.

Updating the trie on every search causes write contention and will not scale. Batch rebuild alone leaves trends stale. Hybrid: immutable trie for >99% of traffic plus a streaming trending overlay merged at query time.

Global top-K is cacheable and CDN-friendly. Personalized results fragment caches — fetch global top-N, re-rank with user history in a few ms, or personalize only after cache miss / on the logged-in path.

Custom trie gives lowest latency and full control but you own sharding and deploy. ES completion suggester (in-memory FST) ships faster with fuzzy/context options and is a good Path-B when a cluster already exists.

gotchas.correction: Too slow and not ranked; needs a prefix index plus precomputed top-K.
Interviewer will ask complexity under prefix "a"; without per-node top-K, short prefixes explode.

gotchas.trap: Updating the trie synchronously on every search
gotchas.correction: Couples write amplification to the latency path; prefer async rebuild and/or a streaming overlay.
QPS can jump 5–10×; clients must debounce (~100–300 ms) and abort stale in-flight responses.

gotchas.trap: Personalizing every response through the edge cache
gotchas.correction: Personalized responses rarely edge-cached; separate global vs personalized paths.

gotchas.trap: Putting typos / fuzzy matching in the MVP
gotchas.correction: Out of MVP; add edit-distance / a separate spell service or ES fuzzy completion only if asked.
Bots can inflate counts; need rate limits and trusted-session filters on the ranking pipeline, plus velocity/uniqueness checks on trending.
REST/HTTP AJAX is fine; WebSocket is rarely needed for typeahead.
